# Command parity and promotion ledger

<!-- Generated by tools/command_promotion.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

The maintained command contract is the live catalog at [`../../src/WinCare.CommandCatalog/Data/commands.json`](../../src/WinCare.CommandCatalog/Data/commands.json). This file is derived from it, so it cannot drift from the contract it describes.

## Why this ledger exists

`docs/Validation.md` makes production promotion conditional on every command reaching `BehaviorVerified`, and `tools/finalize_native_release.py` exits non-zero until that holds. The progress toward that gate was previously narrated in prose with no artifact behind it. This ledger is that artifact: regenerate it with `python tools/command_promotion.py --emit` and verify it in CI with `--check`.

## Promotion ladder

Stages are cumulative. A command listed at a stage has satisfied every weaker stage as well.

| Stage | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Cataloged` | The legacy command is cataloged for migration. |
| `ContractVerified` | The command contract has been verified. |
| `Implemented` | The native implementation is available. |
| `BehaviorVerified` | Native behavior has been verified against the legacy command. |

## Promoting a command

1. Execute the command on a supported Windows host and compare its observable effect against the legacy behavior recorded in `migration/oracle`.
2. Record the result, then set that command's `migrationStatus` to `BehaviorVerified` in the catalog.
3. Run `python tools/command_promotion.py --emit` to refresh this ledger.

A command is only promoted on evidence from a real host. A command that is unreachable, destructive on this machine, or only exercisable with hardware that is absent stays at its current stage and is called out in review rather than promoted on the strength of its unit tests.
